shorts.title: What you will learn: Pass by reference
shorts.hook: One ampersand turns a copy into the real thing.
shorts.script: One ampersand turns a copy into the real thing. Today we fix the broken swap. One small symbol, the ampersand, lets a function change the original. A reference is another name for an existing variable. You write an ampersand after the type. No copy is made. When a function takes a reference, it works on the original variable. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Pass by reference.

shorts.title: Pass by reference in one minute
shorts.hook: A reference is another name for an existing variable.
shorts.script: A reference is another name for an existing variable. You write an ampersand after the type. No copy is made. When a function takes a reference, it works on the original variable. Think of a nickname. Two names point to the same person. The ampersand after int makes n a reference. N is another name for the caller variable. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: PASS BY REFERENCE IN ONE MINUTE
shorts.caption: Pass by reference in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: Both parameters are references. The helper box t keeps the old value of a. A takes the value of b. B takes the old value from t. Now main prints two and one. The swap worked. The C plus plus library also has a function called swap. The program prints two and one. An ampersand after the type makes a reference. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A number cannot be a reference
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. We call inc with the plain number five. The compiler says it cannot bind a non-const lvalue reference to an rvalue. In simple words, five has no box to change. Pass a variable instead. A reference must refer to a real variable. The plain number five has no box that the function could change. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: A reference told a variable, I will always have your back. The variable said, I know, you are my alias.
shorts.script: A reference told a variable, I will always have your back. The variable said, I know, you are my alias. Write a function that takes two int references and doubles both. Test it in main. Write your answer in the comments. An ampersand after the type makes a reference. A reference is another name for the same variable. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
